name: bm-r1-published-tissue-baseline
title: Reduced-order tissue-mechanics baseline
question: How do basement-membrane stiffness and relaxation, relative to the proliferation (doubling) time, control growth-dependent epithelial confinement?
hypothesis: Reimplementing the paper's fixed-volume prism / surface-tension tissue model with a viscoelastic BM reproduces Figure 1G's four stiffness-relaxation regimes and the 1H-J confinement trajectories, with the regime boundary set by the ratio of BM relaxation time to doubling time.
objective: Reimplement the paper's fixed-volume prism/surface-tension tissue model and viscoelastic BM; sweep relative stiffness and the relaxation/doubling-time ratio; compare qualitatively and quantitatively to Barrientos et al. Figure 1G-J.
description:
Direct reproduction of the paper's homogeneous tissue-mechanics result (Barrientos Fig 1). A
fixed-volume prism/surface-tension cell model is coupled to a viscoelastic BM; the relative
BM stiffness and the relaxation/doubling-time ratio are swept to recover the regime topology
(reconstructed basal area and cell height, reversibility, regime boundaries). This is the P1
homogeneous reference the spatial Tyssue studies (R4-R5) are later compared against; it uses
an effective constitutive BM, not the explicit collagen network.

expected_behavior.name: tissue-regimes-match-fig1g
expected_behavior.rationale: Recovering Fig 1G's qualitative regime topology and 1H-J trajectories (within documented numerical tolerances) is the gating success criterion for P1.

baseline.name: bm-r1-published-tissue-baseline
baseline.note: Implemented as a reduced-order homogeneous tissue model (TissuePrismProcess): a fixed-volume prism cell whose basal area is set by proliferation against a viscoelastic BM (stiffness + relaxation). Resolves ready and RUNS; the Fig 1 confinement regimes separate (verified: stiff/slow-relaxing BM -> confined, taller cell; soft/fast -> spread, flatter). The homogeneous effective-BM reference for R4/R5; sweeping stiffness x relaxation/doubling reproduces the Fig 1G regime map (the study's phase-diagram figure).

config.title: Confinement regimes — cell height vs BM stiffness × relaxation (Fig 1G reproduction)
config.caption: REAL run (Barrientos Fig 1G reproduction): cell height swept over BM stiffness × relaxation/doubling from the reduced-order prism model. The confinement regime topology emerges — tall (confined) in the stiff, slowly-relaxing corner.
